title: Weather, nature & seasons
goal: Talk about the weather and seasons, describe nature, and say what looks likely to happen ('it's going to rain').
intro:
Karnataka's geography is varied: the rainy, forested Western Ghats and Malnad (ಮಲೆನಾಡು), the coast (ಕರಾವಳಿ) with heavy monsoons, and the dry Deccan plateau (ಬಯಲುಸೀಮೆ) where Bengaluru's famously pleasant climate sits at 900 m. Talking about the rain is as much a national pastime here as in Britain.

Kannada weather expressions are vivid: rain 'comes' (ಮಳೆ ಬರುತ್ತೆ) and cold 'happens to you' (ಚಳಿ ಆಗುತ್ತೆ). You'll also learn to express predictions: 'it looks like...' and 'it might...'.

phrases.en: It looks like it's going to rain.

grammar.title: Weather expressions: rain 'comes', cold 'happens'
grammar.body:
Weather is expressed with ordinary verbs used impersonally (the weather word is the subject, verb in the neuter ಅದು form):
• **ಮಳೆ ಬರು** 'rain comes': ಮಳೆ ಬರ್ತಿದೆ 'it's raining', ಮಳೆ ಬಂತು 'it rained', ಮಳೆ ನಿಂತಿತು 'the rain stopped'
• **ಗಾಳಿ ಬೀಸು** 'wind blows': ಗಾಳಿ ಬೀಸ್ತಿದೆ
• **ಇದೆ** for states: ಬಿಸಿಲು ಇದೆ 'it's sunny', ಮೋಡ ಇದೆ 'it's cloudy', ಚಳಿ ಇದೆ 'it's cold'

How **you** feel the weather uses the dative + ಆಗು: ನನಗೆ ಚಳಿ ಆಗ್ತಿದೆ 'I'm cold', ಅವರಿಗೆ ಸೆಕೆ ಆಗ್ತಿದೆ 'they're hot'.

Intensity: **ಜೋರಾಗಿ** 'strongly, heavily' (ಜೋರಾಗಿ ಮಳೆ ಬರ್ತಿದೆ 'it's pouring'), **ಸ್ವಲ್ಪ** 'a little'. Adverbs in **-ಆಗಿ / -ಗೆ** describe how something is: ತಣ್ಣಗೆ ಇದೆ 'it's cool', ಬೆಚ್ಚಗೆ ಇದೆ 'it's warm'.

examples.en: In the monsoon it rains every day.
The rain has stopped, let's go.
It's usually a bit cold in the morning.

grammar.title: 'It's going to...', 'it might...', 'it seems...'
grammar.body:
Kannada has no special 'going to' tense; use the present-future (ನಾಳೆ ಮಳೆ ಬರುತ್ತೆ 'it'll rain tomorrow') or one of these:

• **verb (-ಉವ / spoken -ಓ) + ಹಾಗಿದೆ** 'looks like it will': ಮಳೆ ಬರುವ ಹಾಗಿದೆ / ಬರೋ ಹಾಗಿದೆ 'it looks like rain'. ಹಾಗೆ means 'like, in that way'.
• **infinitive + -ಬಹುದು** 'may, might': ಮಳೆ ಬರಬಹುದು 'it may rain', ತಡ ಆಗಬಹುದು 'it might be late'.
• **ಅನ್ನಿಸು** 'seem': sentence + **ಅಂತ ಅನ್ಸುತ್ತೆ** 'I think, it seems': ಮಳೆ ಬರುತ್ತೆ ಅಂತ ಅನ್ಸುತ್ತೆ 'I think it'll rain'. ಅಂತ marks the quoted thought (more in unit 14).

The ending -ಉವ (-ಓ) is the **relative participle**: ಬರುವ 'which comes', ಮಾಡುವ 'which does'. You'll meet it fully in unit 20.

examples.native: ಗುಡುಗು ಬರ್ತಿದೆ, ಜೋರಾಗಿ ಮಳೆ ಬರೋ ಹಾಗಿದೆ
examples.roman: guḍugu bartide, jōrāgi maḷe barō hāgide
examples.en: There's thunder, it looks like heavy rain.
It might get cold in the evening, take a sweater.
It seems the summer is hotter this year.

dialogue.title: A trip to the hills
dialogue.setting: Friends Nikhil and Asha plan a weekend trip to Chikkamagaluru in the Western Ghats.

lines.speaker: Asha
lines.en: Shall we go to Chikkamagaluru this weekend?

lines.speaker: Nikhil
lines.native: ಈಗ ಮಳೆಗಾಲ ಅಲ್ವಾ? ಅಲ್ಲಿ ತುಂಬಾ ಮಳೆ ಬರುತ್ತೆ.
lines.roman: īga maḷegāla alvā? alli tumbā maḷe barutte.
lines.en: It's the monsoon now, isn't it? It rains a lot there.

lines.speaker: Asha
lines.native: ಅದಕ್ಕೇ ಹೋಗಬೇಕು! ಮಳೆಯಲ್ಲಿ ಬೆಟ್ಟ, ಕಾಡು ತುಂಬಾ ಸುಂದರವಾಗಿರುತ್ತೆ.
lines.roman: adakkē hōgabēku! maḷeyalli beṭṭa, kāḍu tumbā sundaravāgirutte.
lines.en: That's exactly why we should go! The hills and forests are beautiful in the rain.

lines.speaker: Nikhil
lines.native: ಹೌದು, ಆದರೆ ಅಲ್ಲಿ ತುಂಬಾ ಚಳಿ ಇರುತ್ತೆ.
lines.roman: haudu, ādare alli tumbā chaḷi irutte.
lines.en: True, but it'll be very cold there.

lines.speaker: Asha
lines.native: ಸ್ವೆಟರ್, ಛತ್ರಿ ತಗೊಂಡು ಹೋಗೋಣ. ಬಿಸಿ ಬಿಸಿ ಕಾಫಿ ಕುಡಿಯೋಣ!
lines.roman: sveṭar, chhatri tagoṇḍu hōgōṇa. bisi bisi kāphi kuḍiyōṇa!
lines.en: Let's take sweaters and umbrellas. We'll drink piping hot coffee!

lines.speaker: Nikhil
lines.native: ಸರಿ. ಆದರೆ ಶನಿವಾರ ಜೋರು ಮಳೆ ಬರಬಹುದು ಅಂತ ನ್ಯೂಸಲ್ಲಿ ಹೇಳಿದ್ರು.
lines.roman: sari. ādare shanivāra jōru maḷe barabahudu anta nyūsalli hēḷidru.
lines.en: Okay. But the news said there might be heavy rain on Saturday.

lines.speaker: Asha
lines.native: ಪರವಾಗಿಲ್ಲ. ಭಾನುವಾರ ಬಿಸಿಲು ಇರುತ್ತೆ ಅಂತ ಅನ್ಸುತ್ತೆ.
lines.roman: paravāgilla. bhānuvāra bisilu irutte anta ansutte.
lines.en: Never mind. I think Sunday will be sunny.

culture: Karnataka is India's biggest coffee producer, grown in the misty hills of Chikkamagaluru, Kodagu (Coorg) and Hassan. The Kaveri (ಕಾವೇರಿ) river, which rises in Kodagu, is revered as a mother goddess, and its water is a subject of deep emotion and politics. Bengaluru was once called the 'Garden City' and is famous for its flowering trees: purple jacaranda and yellow tabebuia in spring.

tip.title: Rain "comes", sun "is"
tip.body:
- The weather word is the subject and the verb takes the **ಅದು** ending: ಮಳೆ **ಬರ್ತಿದೆ** 'it's raining (rain is coming)', ಗಾಳಿ **ಬೀಸ್ತಿದೆ** 'the wind is blowing'.
- States use **ಇದೆ**: ಬಿಸಿಲು ಇದೆ 'it's sunny', ಮೋಡ ಇದೆ 'it's cloudy'; usually: **ಇರುತ್ತೆ**.
- **ಜೋರಾಗಿ** 'heavily', ಸ್ವಲ್ಪ 'a little'.

sentences.en: It's very cloudy today.
It's pouring, come inside.
It's not raining, let's go.
It isn't sunny today.
It's very windy outside.
What's the weather like in Mysuru?

sentences.native: ಈಗ ಬೆಂಗಳೂರಿನಲ್ಲಿ ಪ್ರತಿದಿನ ಸಂಜೆ ಮಳೆ ಬರುತ್ತೆ.
sentences.roman: īga beṅgaḷūrinalli pratidina sañje maḷe barutte.
sentences.en: These days it rains every evening in Bengaluru.
It's usually very sunny in the afternoon.

tip.title: "To me cold is happening"
tip.body:
- How **you** feel the weather: person + **-ಗೆ** + ಚಳಿ / ಸೆಕೆ + **ಆಗ್ತಿದೆ**: ನನಗೆ ಚಳಿ ಆಗ್ತಿದೆ 'I'm cold'.
- ನಿಮಗೆ, ಅವರಿಗೆ, ಅಮ್ಮನಿಗೆ … the verb never changes. Not cold: **ಆಗ್ತಿಲ್ಲ**.
- How something feels: **ತಣ್ಣಗೆ** ಇದೆ 'it's cool', **ಬೆಚ್ಚಗೆ** ಇದೆ 'it's warm'.

sentences.en: Mum is feeling cold.
Are you feeling hot?
I'm not cold, it's fine.
They'll feel cold, shut the door.
It's warm inside the house.
The water is very cold in the morning.

sentences.native: ಮಳೆಯಲ್ಲಿ ನನ್ನ ಬಟ್ಟೆ ಎಲ್ಲಾ ಒದ್ದೆ ಆಯ್ತು.
sentences.roman: maḷeyalli nanna baṭṭe ellā odde āytu.
sentences.en: All my clothes got wet in the rain.
Put the wet clothes outside.

tip.title: Might, looks like, I think
tip.body:
- **-ಬಹುದು** 'may, might': ಮಳೆ ಬರ**ಬಹುದು** 'it might rain'.
- **-ಓ ಹಾಗಿದೆ** 'looks like it will': ಮಳೆ **ಬರೋ ಹಾಗಿದೆ** 'it looks like rain'.
- Whole sentence + **ಅಂತ ಅನ್ಸುತ್ತೆ** 'I think, it seems': ಮಳೆ ಬರುತ್ತೆ ಅಂತ ಅನ್ಸುತ್ತೆ.
- For a plain forecast just use the future: ನಾಳೆ ಮಳೆ ಬರುತ್ತೆ.

sentences.en: The sky has gone dark, it might rain.
There's thunder and lightning, don't go out.
It might rain heavily tonight.
It might be sunny tomorrow.
It looks like it will be very hot today.
It looks like the rain is going to stop.

sentences.native: ಮಳೆ ಬರುತ್ತೆ ಅಂತ ಅನ್ಸುತ್ತೆ, ಛತ್ರಿ ತಗೊಳ್ಳಿ.
sentences.roman: maḷe barutte anta ansutte, chhatri tagoḷḷi.
sentences.en: I think it's going to rain, take an umbrella.
I don't think it'll rain today.
There are lots of stars in the night sky.
The moon is behind a cloud.
The sun is really strong today.
It's very cold up in the hills.
Let's go to Nandi Hills on Sunday.
It might be cloudy up on the hill tomorrow.
Mangaluru is by the sea.
The sea water is really warm.
The Kaveri is a big river in Karnataka.
There's a lot of water in the river now.
There are lots of trees in the forest.
Don't go into the forest at night.
It's cool under that tree.
There's a bird in the tree.

sentences.native: ನಮ್ಮ ಮನೆ ಹತ್ತಿರ ತುಂಬಾ ಹಕ್ಕಿಗಳು ಇವೆ.
sentences.roman: namma mane hattira tumbā hakkigaḷu ive.
sentences.en: There are lots of birds near our house.
Mum loves flowers.

sentences.native: ಈ ಕೆಂಪು ಹೂವು ತುಂಬಾ ಚಂದ ಇದೆ.
sentences.roman: ī kempu hūvu tumbā chanda ide.
sentences.en: This red flower is really pretty.
It's very hot and sticky in summer.
In the monsoon the forest is very green.
Winter mornings are very cold.
Which season do you like?
I love the rainy season.
Summer came early this year.
In the monsoon always take an umbrella with you.
Winter in Bengaluru is lovely.
